_comment: Template for OBJECT_CAROUSEL: a fixed set of files repeated on a cycle, for
rt-mbs-application-provider. Loaded twice, like every template here: once on the MBS User
Services card, which reads the 'service' block, and once on the Ingest Sessions card with
that service open, which reads the 'sessions' array. See templates/README.md.
Use this mode when every receiver should end up with the same set of files and may join at
any moment. Because the set repeats, a receiver that misses an object gets it on the next
cycle; that is what the repetition buys, and it is why the mode costs bearer capacity in
proportion to how often the set repeats.
_subscription: Optional. When present, loading this template on the Ingest Sessions card prefills the Status
Subscription form beneath it -- the notification URI, and the events ticked below. It does not
subscribe: that stays a deliberate, separate step, like creating the service and the session.
A subscription is per Ingest Session, so it cannot be prepared until the session exists, which
is why the form only appears once one has been created.
The events below are the ones that tell you whether delivery actually started, plus the two
failure events that explain a session that never does. Tick more in the form if you want the
full lifecycle; the running MBSF's own list is what the form offers, and an event named here
that it does not offer is reported rather than silently dropped.

_opMode: TS 26.517 V18.6.0 clause 6.2.3.3 defines OBJECT_CAROUSEL. The object list is fixed and
repeated; contrast OBJECT_STREAMING, which follows a presentation manifest and sends each
_acqIds: Every object in the carousel, relative to ingUri, comma-separated. Unlike STREAMING this
is the object list itself, not a manifest to derive one from.
_maxBitrate: A carousel's required rate follows from the set's total size and how often it repeats,
so this is a ceiling rather than a target.
_fecConfig: Optional. Broadcast has no retransmission, so an object is recovered only if every one of
its blocks arrives; FEC adds repair symbols to survive residual loss, at the cost of
bearer capacity. Remove this block for no FEC (Compact No-Code).
